scenarios.title: Valid credentials sign the user in and show the welcome heading
steps: Wait for the h1 to change
expectedResults: The h1 'Welcome back, Demo User' is visible
The form 'Sign in' (email, password fields and submit button) is no longer in the page
No 'Invalid email or password' alert and no field errors are shown
The URL stays /login and the header is unchanged
scenarios.rationale: Core happy path of the only auth flow; verifies the success state replaces the form.

scenarios.title: Submitting the empty form shows both field errors at once
steps: Click the 'Sign in' button without typing anything
expectedResults: 'Enter a valid email address' is shown under the Email field
'Password must be at least 8 characters' is shown under the Password field, both at the same time
Email input has aria-invalid=true and aria-describedby pointing to the element containing the email error; the same for Password
The 'Invalid email or password' alert is not shown
The button still reads 'Sign in' and is enabled (no login request was made, no 500ms loading state)
The h1 remains 'Sign in'
scenarios.rationale: Client-side validation must block the API call and report all problems at once.

scenarios.title: Wrong credentials show a form-level alert, keep the form usable, and replace field errors
steps: Click 'Sign in' with empty fields so both field errors appear
Wait for the button to return to 'Sign in'
Type 'password123' over the password and 'demo@shop.test' over the email, then click 'Sign in'
expectedResults: After the wrong attempt, an alert (role=alert) with 'Invalid email or password' is shown
The two field-level errors are no longer shown (form-level and field-level errors are not displayed together)
The button is enabled again with label 'Sign in'; the entered email and password values are still in the fields
The h1 stays 'Sign in' and no welcome heading appears after the wrong attempt
The corrected credentials then sign in successfully with h1 'Welcome back, Demo User'
scenarios.rationale: Covers the failure path, recovery, and the mutual exclusivity of field and form errors.

scenarios.title: Malformed email addresses are rejected with the email error only
steps: Type 'demo@shop' (no domain suffix) into 'Email' and 'password123' into 'Password', click 'Sign in'
Replace the email with 'demoshop.test' (no @), click 'Sign in'
Replace the email with 'demo @shop.test' (contains a space), click 'Sign in'
expectedResults: After each attempt 'Enter a valid email address' is shown and the email input has aria-invalid=true
'Password must be at least 8 characters' is not shown because the password is valid
No login request is made: the button never shows 'Signing in…' and no 'Invalid email or password' alert appears
The user is not signed in (h1 remains 'Sign in')
scenarios.rationale: Email validation boundaries; noValidate means the browser does not help, so the app rules must hold.

scenarios.title: Password shorter than 8 characters is rejected; exactly 8 characters is accepted for validation
steps: Type 'demo@shop.test' into 'Email' and 'pass123' (7 characters) into 'Password', click 'Sign in'
Replace the password with 'wrongpas' (8 characters), click 'Sign in'
expectedResults: With 7 characters, 'Password must be at least 8 characters' is shown and the email error is not shown; password input has aria-invalid=true; no loading state occurs
With 8 characters the password length error disappears and the login is attempted (button shows 'Signing in…'), ending with the alert 'Invalid email or password' because the credentials are wrong
scenarios.rationale: Boundary test for the 8-character password rule.

scenarios.title: Submit button shows loading state while signing in
steps: Click 'Sign in' and immediately inspect the button
Try to click the button again while it is loading
expectedResults: For about 500ms the button reads 'Signing in…' and is disabled (looks dimmed, not-allowed cursor)
The second click does nothing; only one submission occurs
After the delay the h1 'Welcome back, Demo User' is shown
scenarios.rationale: Loading state prevents duplicate submissions and gives user feedback.

scenarios.title: Email is case-insensitive but password is case-sensitive
steps: Type 'DEMO@SHOP.TEST' into 'Email' and 'password123' into 'Password', click 'Sign in'
Type 'demo@shop.test' into 'Email' and 'Password123' into 'Password', click 'Sign in'
expectedResults: The first attempt signs in: h1 'Welcome back, Demo User' is shown
After reload the sign-in form is shown again (login is not persisted)
The second attempt shows the alert 'Invalid email or password' and no welcome heading
scenarios.rationale: Business rule on credential comparison; also confirms nothing is persisted across reloads.

scenarios.title: Header link opens the sign-in page and the form resets after navigating away
steps: Click the header link 'Sign in to your account'
Verify the page, then sign in with 'demo@shop.test' / 'password123'
Click the header link 'Home', then click 'Sign in to your account' again
expectedResults: The URL is /login and the h1 'Sign in' with labelled 'Email' and 'Password' fields and a 'Sign in' button is visible
After signing in, h1 'Welcome back, Demo User' is shown
After navigating away and back, the sign-in form (h1 'Sign in', empty fields) is shown again, not the welcome heading
scenarios.rationale: Checks entry from the nav and that login state is intentionally not shared or persisted.

scenarios.title: Login form matches the Figma design tokens on desktop
steps: Inspect the 'Sign in' submit button and the form width
expectedResults: h1 'Sign in' uses Inter 700, 40px, line-height 48px
Email and Password inputs are 44px high
The 'Sign in' submit button has background #2563EB, text #FFFFFF, border-radius 8px, height 44px, Inter 16px weight 600, line-height 24px, no border
The form is 400px wide and left-aligned inside the page container, starting 32px below the 64px header
scenarios.rationale: Design fidelity for the Login / Desktop frame (3:53); no reference image, so tokens are checked directly.

scenarios.title: Login page fits a 390px mobile viewport and header nav collapses
steps: Check the header and the page for horizontal scrolling
Check the width of the 'Email' and 'Password' fields and the 'Sign in' button
expectedResults: The header shows a menu toggle button on the right and the nav links are collapsed, as in the Figma mobile header
There is no horizontal scrollbar; document scroll width equals 390px
The inputs and the 'Sign in' button fit within the viewport with the 24px side gutter, stacked vertically, with 44px tall controls
Both validation messages are fully visible and not clipped
The welcome heading 'Welcome back, Demo User' is fully visible without overflow
scenarios.rationale: Mobile usability and header collapse; the page model states the toggle only appears at 320px, which may not match the 390px mobile design (Home / Mobile frame).
